events.title: The Great Surgun
hints: A shah ordered a scorched-earth retreat and a mass deportation during a war with the Ottomans.
Hundreds of thousands were forced to move to central Persia.
The merchants of Julfa were relocated to build a new suburb in Isfahan.
events.summary: During the Ottoman-Safavid war of 1603 to 1618, Shah Abbas I ordered the forced deportation of the population of Eastern Armenia and neighbouring areas to central and northern Persia in 1604 and 1605, a scorched-earth tactic. Around 350,000 people, mostly Armenians, were moved.

events.title: Treaty of Turkmenchay
hints: A war between two empires ended with the transfer of the khanates of Erivan and Nakhchivan in 1828.
Persia also had to pay a large indemnity.
Christians from Persia and the Ottoman lands were encouraged to resettle in the new territory.
events.summary: After the Russo-Persian War of 1826 to 1828, the Treaty of Turkmenchay obliged Persia to cede the Erivan and Nakhchivan khanates to Russia and pay a large indemnity. The Russian government encouraged Armenians from Persia and the Ottoman Empire to resettle in the new territory.

events.title: Russian capture of Erivan
hints: A war between two empires turned decisively in favour of the northern one under a newly arrived general.
An old fortress city was besieged for a week and fell on 1 October 1827.
Its fall opened the road to Tabriz.
events.summary: On 1 October 1827, during the Russo-Persian War of 1826-1828, Russian forces under Ivan Paskevich took Erivan after a siege of about a week, opening the road to Tabriz. The Erivan Khanate was ceded to Russia in 1828 by the Treaty of Turkmenchay.

events.title: Armenian genocide
hints: Deportations and massacres began in April 1915 with the arrest of community leaders in the capital.
Forced marches into the Syrian desert killed vast numbers.
Around a million or more people died, and survivors fled to the Caucasus.
events.summary: From 1915 the Ottoman government carried out mass deportations and killings of its Armenian population, with forced marches into the Syrian desert. An estimated one to one and a half million died, and many survivors fled to the Caucasus, including the territory of the modern republic.

events.title: Soviet invasion and Sovietization
hints: A short-lived republic collapsed after a war with a neighbour and an invasion from the north in late 1920.
The Red Army entered in December 1920.
A February 1921 rebellion against the new government was crushed.
events.summary: After a defeat in a war with Turkish nationalists in autumn 1920, the Armenian republic faced the Red Army, which entered in December 1920 and installed a Soviet government. A rebellion in February 1921 was suppressed, and the republic joined the Transcaucasian federation.
